01 — Visual north star

What this brand must feel like

The brand should feel like: A late-night spot on Route 1 North — dark interior, warm pendant glow, a Spicy Pho Ti-Ni on the bar and karaoke warming up in the back. The kind of place you text your group about, not one you find on a recommendation list.

Not like: A clean-lit family restaurant, a fine dining room, or a delivery-first food platform. Nothing white-tablecloth. Nothing that whispers.

One-line visual thesis

Street-born Vietnamese energy — warm, moody, and built for a night out.

02 — Direction mix

Editorial / Human leads

Editorial / Human — 70% Cutting-edge / Innovative — 30%

Editorial / Human at 70% gives the brand warmth, intimacy, and the personality of a local spot you choose by feel. The 30% Cutting-edge / Innovative keeps it from reading as a legacy restaurant — it sharpens the bar identity and makes the digital experience feel current. Equal weight would neutralize both: too polished to feel like a neighborhood spot, too editorial to feel like an innovator.

What this mix prevents

  • Generic food-delivery platform aesthetics — blue links, grey button defaults, white backgrounds
  • Over-produced menus with no atmosphere — all spec, no soul
  • Cold, clinical layouts that kill the late-night bar energy
  • Fine-dining tone that alienates the bar and karaoke crowd
03 — Color system

Dark base. Gold anchor. Crimson accent.

The near-black base and warm brown surface set the moody evening atmosphere that runs through every section. Gold #F2B928 carries all interactive weight and editorial emphasis; crimson #C23528 appears once — in the bar promo strip.

--base #181008 Page background
--core #241810 Surface (cards section fills): Dark warm brown —
--base-deep #5C4232 Alt section band
--ink #F0E8D0 Primary text
--ink-soft #A08060 Text muted: Warm tan —
--anchor #F2B928 Brand anchor, CTA, dark sections
--anchor-hover #E0A820 Anchor hover
--base-wash #F2B92812 Anchor-tinted band
--accent #C23528 Primary accent
--accent-deep #A82E22 Accent hover / pressed
--neon-0 #52E074 Neon signature (logo / brand mark only):

Usage ratio

The 65 / 20 / 10 / logo-only usage ratio ensures the page reads as warm dark editorial. Gold earns its pop because near-black outnumbers it three to one.

65% Neutrals20% Gold anchor10% Crimson

Never do this

  • Never use white or light grey as a page background — the near-black base is not optional
  • Never apply crimson #C23528 outside the bar promo strip and secondary CTA states
  • Never use neon green #52E074 outside the logo/brand mark
  • Never introduce a fourth accent color or any shade of blue or purple
  • Never render the gold CTA on a light surface — it requires the near-black base to hold contrast
04 — Typography system

Be Vietnam Pro leads. Cormorant Garamond accents.

Be Vietnam Pro carries roughly 90% of the visual work — body text, navigation, labels, and all short-form copy in Bold weight for headings. Cormorant Garamond Italic at display scale handles the hero tagline and one section separator — no more than two moments per page. Together they deliver contemporary editorial warmth: functional at a menu scan, striking when it counts.

05 — Layout rhythm

Immersive narrative scroll.

Each section is a full-width scene, not a card-in-grid module — the page builds from hero atmosphere through food and bar identity to a clear booking moment. It must not feel like a restaurant aggregator listing or a multi-column grid of equal-weight blocks.

Section banding sequence

Full-bleed dark interior — Cormorant Garamond Italic tagline, dual CTAs above fold
Menu highlights
3-column card grid — pho, broken rice, cocktails on surface background
Bar promo strip

Proof band

CTA close
Book a Party — single gold button on dark base, above footer

Alternating — dark full-bleed and slightly lighter card sections

Section patterns used

  • Full-width narrative bands for hero and atmosphere — no container padding, full viewport width
  • 3-column card grid (menu items) on desktop; single column on mobile
  • Proof band — horizontal review strip with Google stars and a short quote
  • Featured quote section — large Cormorant Garamond quote mark, one 5-star review at full scale
  • CTA band — full-width, single gold button, always above the footer

07 — Proof presentation

Let the reviews and the room do the talking.

Quán Phở carries medium trust burden — the brand incorporated March 2025, has fewer than a dozen Yelp reviews, and the bar and karaoke offering isn't visible on the current site. Proof must be front-loaded, specific, and drawn only from confirmed sources.

Phase 1 — Launch

What's confirmed and live

  • 3 × 5-star Google reviews featured on homepage
  • Yelp 4.0★ badge and review count
  • Free spring roll bar promo strip
  • Saturday karaoke at 8PM callout
  • Formerly Long's Noodle House lineage as trust copy

Phase 2 — 3–6 months

Collect and surface

  • Party booking testimonials once booking flow is live
  • Bar and karaoke crowd photos — social energy shots
  • Press or food blogger mentions if obtained
  • Yelp volume growth — target 25+ before featuring count prominently

What must never be fabricated

  • Never write a review, quote, or star rating not sourced from a confirmed Yelp or Google review
  • Never state a Yelp rating above 4.0 — confirmed current rating is 4.0★ (9 reviews)
  • Never add delivery copy until the client confirms a delivery platform and zone
  • Never reference a party booking URL or form until the booking flow is built and confirmed
  • Never imply seating capacity, pricing tier, or private dining setup without client confirmation
08 — Imagery and art direction

The room first. The food second. The crowd third.

Photography direction

Photography directionEnvironment-led + Product-led + People-led
Subject priorityPlace (bar, interior atmosphere) first; Product (food close-ups) second; People (group bar energy) third
MoodWarm, Intimate, Energetic — evening atmosphere
LightingMoody — existing dark high-quality interior shots are the reference standard; warm overhead pendants, not studio white
CompositionClose-up for food; medium-wide for interior/bar; candid-to-documentary for people at the bar
Illustration / icon directionNone — photo-only; full photo library confirmed

Never use these

  • Never use stock photography — the confirmed photo library (13 food shots + 3 interior shots) is the only approved source
  • Never use bright studio-white or daylight photography — the brand lives in evening atmosphere
  • Never use emojis or food icons in place of real photography
  • Never apply heavy filters or oversaturation — the existing dark moody tones are already calibrated
  • Never use a pho bowl on white background as a hero image — reserve food-only shots for menu card context
  • Never introduce people photography that reads as models or stock — candid bar crowd energy only
  • Never apply parallax scroll effects to interior or hero photography
09 — Motion and interaction

Restrained. Purposeful. Never decorative.

Motion rules

LevelRestrained
RoleReveal + Hover
Scroll behaviorFade-up — sections fade in from 12px below, 300ms ease; not staggered; not dramatic
Button hoverGold #F2B928 dims to #E0A820, 150ms ease transition; no scale transform, no glow
Reduced motionRequired — all scroll animations must respect prefers-reduced-motion

What must never animate

  • Never animate text letter-by-letter or word-by-word — no typewriter effects
  • Never apply parallax scroll effects to any image or background
  • Never loop background video or auto-playing animations without a user-pause control
  • Never scale, bounce, or glow CTA buttons on hover — gold dims to #E0A820 only, no transforms
  • Never use looping decorative animations — the brand is warm and settled, not playful
  • Never add number-count animations or progress bars — not supported by current proof assets

Easing curves

--ease: cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1) — UI transitions

--ease-soft: cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) — scroll reveals

11 — Do / Don't rules

Blunt. Visual. Operational.

Do

  • Use existing dark moody interior photography as the visual anchor for every atmospheric section
  • Name the cocktail and dishes specifically in callouts — "Spicy Pho Ti-Ni," not "signature cocktail"
  • Put the gold CTA button above the fold on every major section
  • Show both CTAs (Order Now + Book a Party) in the hero — both are live
  • Use Be Vietnam Pro Bold for all short-sentence copy
  • Keep the bar promo strip (free spring roll) visible early in the page flow
  • Signal Saturday karaoke night with its own dedicated section or callout
  • Use warm gold `#F2B928` for all interactive emphasis — one accent color, consistently applied
  • Allow photography to breathe — generous padding on the dark base
  • Use "formerly Long's Noodle House" lineage as trust copy

Don't

  • Don't use red as the dominant color on any page — crimson belongs to accent and bar promo strip only
  • Don't add delivery copy until confirmed by client
  • Don't use any stock photography — the existing photo library is the asset
  • Don't use a light or white background on any full-page section
  • Don't introduce a third typeface — Be Vietnam Pro + Cormorant Garamond is the complete system
  • Don't use emojis, fire icons, or "hot items" callouts in the UI
  • Don't use the neon green `#52E074` outside the logo mark
  • Don't use "authentic" as a standalone descriptor — replace with the specific dish or tradition
  • Don't apply parallax effects to the hero image
  • Don't add language switcher without confirmed bilingual content need

13 — Implementation notes

What must be preserved. What can flex.

Must preserve exactly

  • Cormorant Garamond Italic at 64px+ in gold #F2B928 for the hero tagline — never swap this font or color
  • Bar promo strip in crimson #C23528 as the single red-dominant section — no other section uses this background color at full width
  • Both CTAs (Order Now + Book a Party) in the hero above the fold — neither is optional
  • Formerly Long's Noodle House lineage copy in the credential bar — exact phrasing preserved
  • Neon green #52E074 strictly in the logo/brand mark only — never in body copy, buttons, or decoration
  • Be Vietnam Pro Bold (700) for all headings and short-copy moments — weight 700 only for titles
  • Alternating section rhythm: base (#181008) → surface (#241810) → crimson strip once → back to base

Accessibility

  • Maintain WCAG AA contrast for all body text: warm cream #F0E8D0 on near-black #181008 — do not lighten the base or darken the text
  • Respect prefers-reduced-motion — all fade-up scroll reveals must be disabled or reduced to instant opacity change for motion-sensitive users
  • Gold #F2B928 on #181008 passes AA for large text (24px+) only — do not use gold for body-size text below 18px
  • All photography must carry meaningful alt text describing scene and subject — not generic filenames or empty strings
  • Buttons must have visible focus rings — use outline: 2px solid #F2B928 on :focus-visible
  • Navigation links must meet 44px minimum tap target height on mobile
  • Do not rely on color alone to communicate state — pair star ratings and status chips with visible text labels

Future agents must never improvise

  • Never introduce a third typeface — Be Vietnam Pro + Cormorant Garamond is the complete and locked typographic system
  • Never change the base background from near-black #181008 to any light, white, or neutral tone
  • Never apply crimson #C23528 as a section background color except in the single bar promo strip
  • Never add delivery copy, pricing, party booking URLs, or seating capacity without explicit client confirmation
  • Never use neon green #52E074 outside the logo mark — it is a brand mark element only, never a UI color
